messages:
Alex K: Heads-up — a customer onboarding just reported duplicate webhook events and signature failures after our last KMS rotation. They see repeated 500s on our side, then multiple retries from their SIEM.
Maria L: Ugh. Do we have any recent schema changes? duplicates could be from acking semantics or retries with no idempotency.
Alex K: No schema changes AFAIK. They mentioned the webhook consumer is Splunk via HTTP Event Collector. They pasted one example where signature header mismatched during key rotation.
Jonah P: Two things to check: 1) webhook delivery ack status handling (we should accept 200/204 only), 2) include a key-id header so consumers can map signature to KMS key during rotation.
Maria L: Agree. We should add an "X-Redwood-Key-Id" header on every webhook, and rotate: sign with new key but keep old key valid for N hours for replay window. Also include an idempotency token in the payload metadata.
Alex K: Proposed header plan:

```
X-Redwood-Signature: sha256=...
X-Redwood-Key-Id: rk-2026-05-01
X-Redwood-Event-Id: evt_abc123
```

And we should document that consumer must respond with 2xx to acknowledge; anything else triggers exponential backoff and eventual S3 fallback.
Ops SRE: For backpressure, we already have a per-customer queue and a retry backoff. But we don't surface the ack vs retry count to customers currently.
Maria L: We should add a small "delivery_metadata" section in the audit event with: attempt_number, last_attempt_ts, last_http_status, and fallback_destination (s3/kafka). That lets customers map duplicates.
Jonah P: Careful — audit schema change must be versioned. Add a top-level "schema_version": "audit.v3" and keep previous versions supported for 30 days. Also publish a compatibility matrix.
Alex K: Good. Customer-facing validation: provide a small validator endpoint or a sample script they can run to verify signatures. Example consumer snippet:

```
# verify.py
import hmac, hashlib
sig = 'sha256=' + hmac.new(key, body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
assert hmac.compare_digest(sig, header_sig)
```

Include psuedo-code for key selection by X-Redwood-Key-Id.
security-bot: CI job created: `ci/webhook-signature-test` — will run sample payloads against all active KMS keys and ensure both old/new verify for overlapping window.
Maria L: Also need to call out SIEM mapping: for Splunk HEC, customers prefer a flattened event. We should provide both raw audit_event and a flattened_siem wrapper. Example:

```
{ "schema_version": "audit.v3", "event": {...}, "flattened_siem": {"host":"app", "msg":"..."} }
```

Jonah P: On on-boarding docs: add a checklist: shared secret vs public-key verification, expected headers, acceptable status codes, idempotency token semantics, retry window, and fallback URL for S3 export with signed URL delivery.
Alex K: Action items: Maria to draft schema.v3 PR + examples, Jonah to update delivery runtime to emit X-Redwood-Key-Id and delivery_metadata, Ops SRE to confirm retry/backoff surfacing and S3 fallback behavior, and I'll reach out to the customer with a short patch and sample verifier.
Maria L: I'll open the PR today and include a migration guide and tests.
Jonah P: I'll schedule a quick runbook update and add a dashboard for webhook non-2xx rates per customer.
Alex K: Thanks. Ping me when PR is up and I'll coordinate the customer message. :thumbsup:
Maria L: Posted initial PR link — https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4021 (WIP)
Ops SRE: Noted. I'll verify S3 fallback signed URLs expire after 24h and include tenant scoping.
Alex K: Great, closing the loop here. If anyone sees other customers with similar symptoms, tag me and include sample headers.
